requirements.check: Real commit-stage CSR write and port-1 candidate cannot release younger AKV during flush; changing permission in either direction discards old decoded work.
A flushed accelerator transaction ID must not retain permission to release a later speculative instruction.
Older exception and xRET flush queued/decoded AKV; refetch uses the new execution privilege and its own allowance.
An already authorized request is preserved under backpressure across a later gate closure, with exactly one handshake.
Vector CSR drain cannot complete while earlier vector writes remain; distinguish protocol-stub checks from evidence with real backend and VRF.
